![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14097009/assets/ec8492d2d545c54f8af112d2221c09eeb0201ca9cdc199d1c6b2cab768c282ea.png)

The graph of a function $y=f(x)$ is shown above. Given $g(t)={\int }_{-4}^{t}f(x)\,\text{d}x,$ determine the value of $g(1).$
worked_solution:
Evaluating $g(t)$ at $t=1,$ we get the following definite integral:

$$
g(1)={\int }_{-4}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

This integral gives the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14097009/assets/ab9a16779fc4b2d4578df9bbb74c3df34c958bdb2bdd25d5db30910da7f1d9d6.png)

Note that the graph above consists of $2$ parts:

- $x\in [-4,0],$ for which the region between the curve and the $x$-axis is a trapezoid. This corresponds to the area ${A}_{1}.$

- $x\in [0,1],$ for which the region between the curve and the $x$-axis is a rectangle. This corresponds to the area ${A}_{2}.$

Therefore, we can write the integral as follows:

$$
g(1)={\int }_{-4}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-4}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}
$$

Now, let's compute these integrals:

- To find the first integral where $x\in [-4,0],$ we compute the area ${A}_{1}$ of the trapezoid as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4\cdot (1+2) \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

- To find the second integral where $x\in [0,1],$ we compute the area ${A}_{2}$ of the rectangle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =1\cdot 2 \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}g(1)={\int }_{-4}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}=6+2=8.\end{aligned}
$$
